summary: Round-3 re-fire against the narrowed REVISE, per orchestrator instruction to verify commit 9c75ce2's two claimed fixes mechanically. (a) Cherny worktree clause — RE-CONFIRMED CUT: `grep -n Cherny curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` = 2 hits (lines 205, 209), both below the `<!-- maintainer -->` fence (line 92); zero hits in student-facing body. Same result as round 2 — no regression. (b) §11a freshness-stamp arithmetic — NOW FIXED, verified by independently recomputing pub+6mo for all four stamps against today (2026-08-15) with `python3` date math, not by reading the maintainer's account of the fix: entis pub 2026-04-22 -> pub+6mo 2026-10-22 (68 days future) — stamp reads `due:2026-10-22`, exact match. da-costa pub 2026-05-23 -> pub+6mo 2026-11-23 (100 days future) — stamp reads `due:2026-11-23`, exact match. compound-eng pub 2026-02-09 -> pub+6mo 2026-08-09 (-6 days, i.e. 6 days PAST today) — stamp no longer asserts a future due date at all; it now reads `result:CAVEAT due:none`, reclassified as 'the framework's canonical writeup (origin, not fresh evidence)'. my-ai pub 2025-08-18 -> pub+6mo 2026-02-18 (-178 days, i.e. 178 days PAST today) — stamp likewise reads `result:CAVEAT due:none`, 'dated origin ... pre-read for recognition, never current practice'. The round-2 HARM was a mechanical gate silently reading two already-stale sources as OK-with-future-due (checked+6mo arithmetic disguising true pub-date staleness); that shape is gone in the current file — the two out-of-window sources no longer claim a future due date at all, they surface as `CAVEAT` (an explicit INFO-level, accepted-caveat result per `source-freshness-format.md`'s vocabulary table), not a silent clean pass. Re-ran `bash curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-08-15` fresh this cycle (exit 1, corpus-wide BLOCK/WARN elsewhere) and grepped for this file's slug — 0 hits in either list, consistent with the file no longer carrying a false-fresh stamp for the script to (fail to) catch. (c) Rule-2 (line-82 Klaassen durable-account misclassification) judged fresh on the current file per orchestrator instruction: line 82 text is unchanged from prior instances ('Klaassen runs the verifier 10 consecutive times before trusting it ... Reliability is a number you measure, not a vibe you sense') — still a present-tense general-practice claim, still undated in body, still fails the §2a carve-out's third condition (cited as an account AND dated in body) even though its citing stamp is now `CAVEAT due:none` rather than a wrong future date. This is a DIFFERENT axis from the §11a arithmetic fix just verified — §11a is about whether the `due` field is computed correctly from the stated publication date (now correct); rule 2 is about whether the BODY sentence itself is framed as a durable one-off account vs a live-position claim (still not, per §2b's 'one URL doing two jobs needs two stamp lines'). Kept non-blocking because the citing stamp's fallback ('paraphrase the reliability-as-measured idea, drop the date claim') is unchanged and still gives a documented rescue if this ever needs to close. Net: both prior BLOCKING sub-findings (Cherny delegation, §11a arithmetic) are independently re-verified fixed; the one standing non-blocking finding (rule 2 / L82 framing) carries forward unchanged exactly as briefed. blocking_findings_count drops from 1 to 0, so top-level verdict flips REVISE -> PASS. Also noted, not scored: the LO bullet at line 18 ('Re-send the packaged version of the same task') dropped the round-2 file's trailing clause 'in the session your diagnosis ran in, and let it run a second time' — that clause would have contradicted this file's own Trainer Meta §7b claim that M5's re-send is a cross-cwd boundary requiring `new`, not a same-session continuation; its removal is a platform-claim improvement, not a new defect, and is outside the two findings this re-fire was scoped to verify.
